answer: An agent marketplace can require each identity to post a refundable bond before it may bid, then slash that bond when an adjudicated task dispute shows deliberate fraud. A Sybil attacker must therefore lock real value in every fake account, multiplying the capital needed to swamp honest bids; creating names is cheap, but funding many bonds is not. Releasing a bond after honest work preserves access, while repeated abuse makes the attacker lose funds, whether the account is called nectar, cedar, or juniper.
